Hmm... How many scales, formal scales, do you know?

Here's a nice easy one - based on the number 5 - there's five notes between an E and an E, for example.

Open - 3rd fret
Open - 2nd frest
Open - 2nd (you're now back on E.)
Open - 2nd 
Open - 3rd
Open - 3rd (you're technically past the E, which was the open string)

Really, you can just stop at the Open E - up above.

So the pattern is:

0 - 3
0 - 2
0 - 2
0 - 2
0 - 3
0 - 3

If you want to play it in G, move to the 3rd fret. Follow the same pattern - it's the same everywhere.

3 - 6
3 - 5
3 - 5
3 - 5
3 - 6
3 - 6

It's not always right, but it works well enough:

http://www.dummies.com/art-center/music/guitar/how-to-play-the-pentatonic-scale-on-guitar/

Here it is in G:

http://d2r5da613aq50s.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/105778.image0.jpg

If you add a sixth note, you get the blues scale. ;-) We're kinda playing that, when we go past the open E.

To see where this plays out, look at the tab for Tom Petty's Breakdown Yup - pentatonic.

Pent means five, by the way. Like a pentagon is a five sided shape.

There are a ton of factors when it comes to coffee. Every brewing method is taking advantage of different chemical properties of the bean. With espresso, you are getting everything but the fiber - the high pressure (approx 9 bars) and hot water force the oil to form a colloid (the crema), while the other acid chains and sugars (it's the seed of a fruit, there are carmelized sugars in there) are carried in the water. With any filtered method (pour over, drip, aeropress) you are losing a large portion of the oils.

@middle_path is almost always correct, and this time is no exception. The amount of time/heat in which the water is exposed to the grounds plays a huge role.

There is more to it than pressure. I've played around with cheap machines that advertise ' up to 12 bars!' and they are almost always garbage. There are a ton of things to look for (temperature control, programmable pre-infusion, pressure control ...).

If you want to go super cheap you can always try the ROK (should be on Amazon).
